method: Each playing position is a mode of the harp's own major scale. A 10-hole Richter diatonic is tuned to one major scale, so the blow notes are the root, third and fifth of that key and the draw notes the second, fifth, seventh, second, fourth and sixth, repeated over ten holes. 1st position plays the harp's key (Ionian), 2nd position (cross harp) plays a fourth below it (Mixolydian), 3rd another fourth below (Dorian), 4th the sixth degree (Aeolian), 5th the third (Phrygian), 6th the seventh (Locrian) and 7th the fourth (Lydian). The harmonica needed for a song key and position is the harp key whose scale degree for that position lands on the song key: the song pitch class minus the degree's semitone offset (0, 4, 2, 6, 8, 10 or 5 for positions 1 to 7). The page lists the seven scale notes of the chosen position, every blow and draw note of the harp key with the root marked, and the key each of the seven positions plays in on that harp. Notes are spelled in the harp's key by letter and accidental, so a D flat song can read as C sharp on an F sharp harp. Only positions 1 to 7 and the standard 10-hole Richter diatonic are modelled: tremolo, chromatic, minor-tuned and alternate tunings, cross-position bending and overblow technique are outside the model. It stores, uploads and transmits nothing and runs entirely in the browser.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Harmonica: a diatonic harmonica is tuned to a single major scale and players reach other keys by playing in different positions, which are modes of that scale.
Richter tuning reference: the blow notes of a 10-hole diatonic are the root, third and fifth of the harp key and the draw notes are its second, fifth, seventh, second, fourth and sixth.
Harmonica position practice: 1st position is straight harp in the harp key and 2nd position is cross harp a perfect fourth below it, with each further position another fourth down the same scale.
Wikipedia, Mode (music): the seven diatonic modes are rotations of the major scale, each starting on a different degree of it.
